rationale: Two things matter on this model and neither of them is a throughput knob in the usual sense. (1) qwen4_ple_ssd_offload is the residency enabler: the PLE table is 79.2 GB of mmap-able weights and offloading it is what makes a 105 GB checkpoint fit at all. It is also the single biggest performance lever measured here - on a cache-defeated cold ~21.7k-token prefill it is worth 20.5 s of TTFT (33.8 s vs 54.3 s) and 3.8x decode (72.1 vs 19.1 tps), because the alternative is expert offload at 0.61 which is far more expensive per token. (2) enable_thinking: false is the real tuning lever: paired n=10/arm it is +8.0% decode, -275 ms total, +12.6 ms TTFT, and it is the difference between the model emitting reasoning before every answer and not. On this model null is NOT off (1111 reasoning chars, ttfc 4888 ms) and true is byte-identical to null. MTP is worth +59% decode (58.53 -> 93.18 tps) and adaptive depth is the right setting; fixed 2 and fixed 4 are both inside noise of it. MoE expert offload is rejected outright: with PLE offload on the model already fits with zero expert offload, and every expert-offload arm is monotonically worse on both axes - 0.75 resident fraction costs 28% decode and 1.9x TTFT while still being 18 GB larger than the PLE-only arm, and 0.10 costs 7x decode. KV quantization, context window, sampler and temperature are all nulls. force_sampling is a measurement artifact, not a lever. The whole-config gain is +2.5% to +6.2% decode and is dominated by the thinking pin; the two runs disagree by 2.4x, so it is reported as a range and treated as low confidence.
failure_modes: The paged prefix cache serves the entire prefill under measure.py, so TTFT measures cache restore and every prefill knob reads null. Worked around with tuning/coldprefill.py, which prepends a fresh random nonce per request so cached_tokens stays 0. coldprefill.py takes its pad from the PAD env var, not an argument - passing it as an argument silently yields pt=47 and a meaningless result.
The KV skip-last field is turboquant_skip_last, NOT turboquant_kv_skip_last. The latter returns HTTP 422 extra_forbidden. The first KV sweep attempt was lost to this.
GET /admin/api/models/{id}/settings returns 405. Read .settings off GET /admin/api/models instead.
auto_unloaded unloads but does NOT reload. Every reload-requiring PUT must be followed by POST /load and a poll for loaded: true, or the next measurement runs against an empty slot.
ab.py leaves its last patch applied. Reset after every run or the next test starts from the wrong config.

enable_thinking: null is not off on this model. It emitted 1111 reasoning chars with ttfc 4888 ms while ttft looked normal. enable_thinking: true was byte-identical to null. Only explicit false disables thinking.

force_sampling: true overrides the request's temperature 0.0 with the model's configured 0.6, so any temp-0 harness measures a different sampler on that arm. Verified with three identical temp-0 requests: false -> 1/3 distinct outputs, true -> 2/3 distinct.

Per-sample warmup ramps are real and large. The PLE-only arm of the MoE sweep ran 82.3, 79.4, 82.0, 79.2 then 96.8, 97.5, 97.6, 95.8 across its two passes - the first pass was still warming, so its median is conservative. The whole-config blocks show the opposite drift (final-config 95.9 -> 87.0 within one block), so the arm that runs first in a block looks better.
qwen4_ple_ssd_offload_forced read true early in the session and false later. It is a derived flag, not a setting; do not use it to infer whether offload is active - read qwen4_ple_ssd_offload.

The memory ceiling is dynamic and state-dependent: observed 85.93 / 88.81 / 90.95 / 96.3-100.5 / 98.1 / 113.35 / 127.1 GB in different states. Every resident-memory number in this report records the ceiling it was measured against.
measure.py intermittently exits non-zero with no 'run 1:' line. The harnesses retry up to 3x; a single failure is not a config result.
measurement_caveat: No number in this report is comparable to a number from a different block. Absolute decode throughput on this machine drifts 30%+ between sessions with no config change. Every verdict above is a paired comparison inside one block: interleaved A/B (tuning/ab.py) for knobs that do not reload (context window, sampler, temperature, force_sampling); alternating blocks with a discarded warmup per block (tuning/block.py) for knobs that do reload (thinking, MTP depth, KV quant, MoE expert offload, PLE offload, and the whole-config head-to-head); forward-then-backward ordering (tuning/blocksweep.py) for multi-value sweeps. The null spread was measured twice with the identical config in both arms: 0.13% decode / 1.0% TTFT (n=5 x 2 blocks) and 1.0% decode / 0.6% TTFT (n=10 per arm). Treat ~1% as the noise floor; anything at or below it is reported as a null. The whole-config decode delta is +2.5% to +6.2% across two runs of the same test and is partly noise - it is a range, not a point estimate.
